sources.name: DONKI space weather database (via api.nasa.gov)
sources.usedFor: Used in play: 10 real radiation-storm (SEP) events from September 2017 and May 2024, fetched from the DONKI API and saved in the game. Kept as real background facts. Every NASA forecast in the game also asks DONKI live about the last 30 days (solar flares, CMEs, radiation storms) and shows the date it checked.

sources.name: NASA Image and Video Library
sources.usedFor: Used in play: 7 real images (for example 'Dust Storm Covers Opportunity', June 2018, and 'Solar Storm Triggers Whole-Planet Aurora at Mars', 2017) shown in briefings, debriefs and the Crew Handbook, with their titles, dates and credits.

sources.name: NASA 3D Resources (3D models)
sources.usedFor: Used in play: the Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover model is your scout rover, and the Astronaut model is the suit on the suit stand. Logos were removed because our Mission Control is pretend.

sources.name: Opportunity 2018 power data
sources.usedFor: Used in play: the real power and dust (tau) readings for June 3, 4, 6 and 10, 2018 drive the sky and solar power in Stage 1, The Storm.

sources.name: Curiosity Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD)
sources.usedFor: Background reference: RAD measured radiation at the surface of Mars about doubling during the September 2017 solar storm. Not used for numbers in the game.

sources.name: Spirit and Opportunity mission history
sources.usedFor: The real stories behind Stages 2, 3 and 4: Spirit's last winter (2010), Purgatory Dune (2005) and Troy (2009), and solar conjunction.

sources.name: Curiosity rover wheel updates (2013-2017)
sources.usedFor: The real story behind Stage 5, Wheel Trouble: sharp rocks made holes in Curiosity's wheels, and the team changed routes and software.

sources.name: Phoenix Mars Lander ice discovery (2008)
sources.usedFor: The real story behind Stage 6, Ice Hunters: Phoenix dug up water ice near Mars's north pole. The ice map in the game is pretend.

sources.name: MOXIE oxygen experiment on Perseverance (2021-2023)
sources.usedFor: Why ice and air go together in the game: MOXIE really made oxygen on Mars. In the game, ice you dig up becomes extra air the next morning (simulated amounts).

sources.name: Subsurface Water Ice Mapping (SWIM)
sources.usedFor: Background reference on how scientists map buried ice from orbit. The game's ice maps are made up, not real SWIM data.

sources.name: Mars Trek
sources.usedFor: Reference for the landscape: Meridiani Planum's flat plain, small craters and pale bedrock (the game's map is simplified, not an exact copy).

sources.name: RadLab
sources.usedFor: Background reference on how space radiation is measured for astronauts. Not used for numbers in the game.

sources.name: Open Science Data Repository (OSDR)
sources.usedFor: Background reference on astronaut health in space (radiation, oxygen, food). Not used for numbers in the game.

sources.name: Space food toolkit
sources.usedFor: Background reference for the food counter and greenhouse. Not used for numbers in the game.
